style: Original illustration made to look like a hand-printed RISOGRAPH poster: only four flat spot inks — fluorescent orange, deep federal-blue/navy, warm mustard yellow and off-black — on cream uncoated paper. Visible coarse halftone dots, slight misregistration between ink layers (1-2 mm offset), uneven ink coverage, paper grain and tiny dust specks. Drawing done with confident brush-and-ink linework like a traditional Korean folk painting (minhwa) woodblock: the tiger has the old minhwa character — big round goggle eyes, wide toothy comical grin, bold blunt stripes, chunky stylised paws — drawn as flat shapes, not realistic fur. People drawn simply with few lines, matte flat color, small simple faces. Composition asymmetric and graphic with generous negative space; strong silhouette readable from far. Leave the top 24% of the frame as flat dark navy ink with only a little texture (title space) and keep the bottom 9% flat navy too. AVOID: glossy highlights, 3D rendering, airbrushed gradients, oversaturated neon, bokeh, lens flare, perfectly symmetrical layout, plastic-looking skin, excessive micro-detail, cluttered backgrounds. ABSOLUTELY NO text, letters, numbers, signage writing, fake glyphs, watermarks, logos or app interface anywhere; phone screens are plain flat yellow-white light. Hands simple with correct finger count or hidden in pockets/sleeves. Not in the style of any specific artist.

images.en: A steep zigzag stairway in an old hillside Seoul neighbourhood at night, seen from slightly below and to the left. Small flat-roofed houses with rooftop water tanks stacked up the hill, a few thin power lines. One tired young office worker in a long padded coat climbs the stairs, head bowed into the glowing phone held in both hands. On three landings going up (big in the foreground right, medium in the middle, small near the top) sits the same grinning minhwa tiger wearing an oversized hoodie, each one holding out a paw palm-up, and each already holding one round white rice cake (tteok). Her open tote bag shows only two rice cakes left; a few rice-cake crumbs on the steps. A big flat full moon sits off-centre in the navy sky.

Close, intimate view inside a tiny one-room flat at 2 AM: a young person lies on their side in bed under a thick duvet, only face and one hand holding a phone visible, face lit by the phone's flat yellow-white light. Out of the phone screen — as if the screen were a small doorway — a big grinning minhwa tiger in a hoodie leans halfway out, one chunky paw held palm-up just above the pillow, waiting to be given something. On the bedside stool a small plate holds one last round white rice cake (tteok), with empty space where many others were. Behind, a window with a few flat block silhouettes of apartment towers and a moon. Placed off-centre: person lower left, tiger rising toward upper right.
